question: What is the primary purpose of a reproductive physical examination?

options.A: Providing a definitive diagnosis without a patient history
options.B: Identifying anatomical abnormalities and functional disturbances
options.C: Replacing the need for laboratory blood investigations
options.D: Determining the exact genetic makeup of the patient

explanation: The physical examination seeks to find objective signs of pathology and structural issues to guide further care. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is recognizing normal anatomical variants important during a reproductive assessment?

options.A: It prevents misdiagnosis and reduces unnecessary patient anxiety
options.B: It eliminates the necessity for standard infection control protocols
options.C: It guarantees that no further imaging studies will be ordered
options.D: It speeds up documentation by bypassing normal findings

explanation: Knowing what is within the range of normal prevents mistaking a benign variant for a disease process. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why should a patient empty their bladder immediately before a reproductive pelvic examination?

options.A: To speed up the overall recovery time post-procedure
options.B: To cause uterine contractions that help visualize the cervix
options.C: To ensure patient comfort and allow accurate pelvic palpation
options.D: To prevent the need for a clean-catch urine specimen collection

explanation: A full bladder causes discomfort and displaces reproductive organs, making manual palpation difficult and unreliable. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h2)

question: A patient appears visibly anxious and tense while climbing onto the examination table. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Explain each step of the procedure and allow them to ask questions
options.B: Proceed rapidly with the exam to minimize the duration of stress
options.C: Insist that a family member leaves the room immediately
options.D: Administer a mild sedative to calm their autonomic nervous system

explanation: Verbal preparation and open communication build trust and significantly reduce procedural anxiety. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h2)

question: What type of lubricant should be selected for a reproductive physical examination involving a speculum?
explanation: Water-soluble lubricants prevent interference with cytologic specimens and do not degrade latex barrier equipment. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following practices is NOT acceptable regarding infection control during pelvic examinations?

options.A: Performing hand hygiene before putting on examination gloves
options.B: Reusing disposable plastic speculums after cold water rinsing
options.C: Placing used needles immediately into a nearby sharps container
options.D: Disinfecting examination lights between different patients

explanation: Disposable equipment is designed for single use only and cannot be safely sterilized with simple rinsing. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which endocrine gland should be palpated during an extrapelvic reproductive assessment due to its link with menstrual irregularities?
explanation: Thyroid disorders directly impact the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, leading to various menstrual and reproductive symptoms. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is the assessment of secondary sexual characteristics and fat distribution included in a reproductive physical exam?

options.A: They replace the need to take a detailed menstrual and obstetric history
options.B: They provide visible clues regarding underlying endocrine and hormonal imbalances
options.C: They confirm the exact chronological age of the adult patient
options.D: They measure the exact functional capacity of the cardiac system

explanation: Hormones dictate the development of secondary sex characteristics, making physical patterns valuable diagnostic indicators. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of bimanual palpation during a female pelvic examination?

options.A: To assess the size, shape, and consistency of the uterus and adnexa
options.B: To measure the exact pH level of vaginal secretions
options.C: To dilate the cervical os prior to an intrauterine device insertion
options.D: To visualize cellular changes on the surface of the uterine cervix

explanation: Bimanual exam uses fingers in the vagina and abdominal hand externally to feel internal pelvic organs. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h5)

question: A patient asks why a speculum is being inserted into her vagina. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: To measure the total depth and elasticity of the uterine muscular walls
options.B: To physically stimulate the release of reproductive hormones
options.C: To collect a baseline sample of urine directly from the bladder
options.D: To safely widen the vaginal canal so the clinician can view the cervix

explanation: The speculum acts as an instrument to retract tissue walls, providing a direct line of sight to the cervix. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h5)

question: What maneuver is commonly used to check for an inguinal hernia during a male reproductive assessment?

options.A: Palpating the abdomen while the patient holds their breath
options.B: Asking the patient to perform deep knee bends
options.C: Measuring the scrotal circumference with a tape measure
options.D: Having the patient turn their head and cough

explanation: Coughing increases intra-abdominal pressure, which forces a hernia sac outward against the examining fingers. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h6)

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to perform a proper testicular self-examination?

options.A: Inspect the scrotal skin using a mirror without touching the organs
options.B: Roll each testicle gently between the thumb and first two fingers
options.C: Press the spermatic cord upward until discomfort occurs
options.D: Squeeze the testicle firmly to test for deep pain reflexes

explanation: Gentle rolling allows the fingers to feel the entire surface of the testis and epididymis for abnormal lumps. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical objective of obtaining a Pap smear during a speculum examination?

options.A: Screening for premalignant cellular changes and cervical cancer
options.B: Evaluating the patency of the fallopian tubes
options.C: Measuring the exact hormone levels circulating in the blood
options.D: Diagnosing a urinary tract infection caused by bacteria

explanation: Cervical cytology examines cells from the transformation zone to detect dysplasia before it progresses to cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h7)

question: When is the most critical time to label a laboratory specimen collected during a reproductive exam?

options.A: Just before the laboratory technician starts processing the sample
options.B: Whenever the laboratory supervisor requests clarification
options.C: After returning to the nursing station at the end of the shift
options.D: At the bedside immediately in the presence of the patient

explanation: Immediate bedside labeling prevents sample mix-ups and ensures absolute patient safety and traceability. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h7)

question: What type of language should a nurse avoid when documenting reproductive physical examination findings?
explanation: Documentation must remain strictly professional, objective, and free from personal opinions or biases. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h8)

question: A nurse discovers a small lesion on the labia during an assessment. Which entry best represents proper documentation?

options.A: Disgusting growth observed on the external genitalia
options.B: Strange sore found on private parts that looks suspicious
options.C: 1 cm ulcerated lesion with raised borders on the left labia majora
options.D: Patient has a bad infection in the genital area that hurts a lot

explanation: Professional documentation uses exact size, description, and location without emotional or derogatory labels. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h8)
